claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis shown in Figure 5 and supplements

claims.claim: The mixed immune cells cluster contained a unique cell type corresponding to dendritic cells.
claims.source: Further analysis of the mixed immune cells cluster showed that it contained a unique cell type with expression of distinct genes compared to microglia or T-cells (e.g. Plbd1, Mgl2, Clec9a) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A). Subclustering of the mixed immune cells identified this unique cell type as a distinct cluster from microglia or T-cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), and mapping onto ImmGen cell type data (Heng and Painter, 2008) revealed this population corresponded to dendritic cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis and ImmGen mapping shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3

claims.claim: Dendritic cells showed an elevation in P301S brains.
claims.source: Like microglia and T-cells, dendritic cells also showed an elevation in P301S brains (Figure 5C; Figure 5—figure supplement 4, C21).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis shown in Figure 5C and supplement

claims.claim: TPL2-KD did not have a significant effect on the proportion of most cell types in non-transgenic mice.
claims.source: Strikingly, while TPL2-KD did not have a significant effect on the proportion of any of the 13 cell types in non-transgenic mice, and did not alter the proportion of most cell types in P301S brains, TPL2-KD significantly reduced the abundance of T-cells and dendritic cells in P301S brains (Figure 5B and C; Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis shown in Figure 5B, C and supplement

claims.claim: TPL2-KD significantly reduced the abundance of T-cells and dendritic cells in P301S brains.
claims.source: Strikingly, while TPL2-KD did not have a significant effect on the proportion of any of the 13 cell types in non-transgenic mice, and did not alter the proportion of most cell types in P301S brains, TPL2-KD significantly reduced the abundance of T-cells and dendritic cells in P301S brains (Figure 5B and C; Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis shown in Figure 5B, C and supplement

claims.claim: P301S;TPL2-KD mice have reduced infiltration of peripheral immune cells compared to P301S mice.
claims.source: This indicates that P301S;TPL2-KD mice have reduced infiltration of peripheral immune cells compared to P301S mice.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the reduced abundance of T-cells and dendritic cells

claims.claim: T-cell number in the fimbria area was increased in TauP301S mouse brains, and the increase was normalized by TPL2-KD.
claims.source: To corroborate the scRNA-seq results, we also performed T-cell immunohistochemistry (IHC) using fixed brain tissue sections. T-cell number in the fimbria area (the area that has the most robust T-cell abundance in previous studies of TauPS2APP mice; Lee et al., 2021b) was increased in TauP301S mouse brains, and the increase was normalized by TPL2-KD (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C).
claims.evidence: Supported by IHC data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C

claims.claim: T-cells are present in the brains of human AD patients and preclinical disease models.
claims.source: Given the presence of T-cells in the brains of human AD patients and preclinical disease models, and the beneficial effects of T-cell depletion in mouse disease or injury models (Chen et al., 2023; Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018; Togo et al., 2002), the decreased presence of peripheral immune cells in TauP301SxTPL2-KD mouse brains could have beneficial effects.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claims.claim: T-cell depletion has beneficial effects in mouse disease or injury models.
claims.source: Given the presence of T-cells in the brains of human AD patients and preclinical disease models, and the beneficial effects of T-cell depletion in mouse disease or injury models (Chen et al., 2023; Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018; Togo et al., 2002), the decreased presence of peripheral immune cells in TauP301SxTPL2-KD mouse brains could have beneficial effects.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Chen et al., 2023; Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018; Togo et al., 2002

claims.claim: The decreased presence of peripheral immune cells in TauP301SxTPL2-KD mouse brains could have beneficial effects.
claims.source: Given the presence of T-cells in the brains of human AD patients and preclinical disease models, and the beneficial effects of T-cell depletion in mouse disease or injury models (Chen et al., 2023; Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018; Togo et al., 2002), the decreased presence of peripheral immune cells in TauP301SxTPL2-KD mouse brains could have beneficial effects.
claims.evidence: Speculative inference based on cited studies

claims.claim: Both CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell numbers were increased in P301S brains, and TPL2-KD significantly reduced the abundance of both cell types.
claims.source: Cellularity analysis showed that both CD4+ and CD8+ cell numbers were increased in P301S brains, and TPL2-KD significantly reduced the abundance of both cell types (Figure 5—figure supplement 5C).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5C

claims.claim: CD8.4, the largest T-cell subcluster, was decreased in P301S;TPL2-KD mouse brains.
claims.source: When the relative abundance was compared within the T-cell population, CD8.4, the largest T-cell subcluster, was decreased in P301S;TPL2-KD mouse brains (Figure 5—figure supplement 5D).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5D

claims.claim: CD8.4 cells expressed marker genes of exhausted T-cells, such as Nr4a2 and Pdcd1.
claims.source: CD8.4 cells expressed some marker genes of exhausted T-cells, such as Nr4a2 and Pdcd1, which are usually induced by chronic/persistent exposure to antigens and/or inflammation (Odagiu et al., 2020; Wherry, 2011; Wherry and Kurachi, 2015; Yi et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq gene expression data and citations

claims.claim: Within the TauP301S group, when comparing TPL2-KD to TPL2-WT mice, differentially expressed genes were only detected in microglia.
claims.source: However, within the TauP301S group, when comparing TPL2-KD to TPL2-WT mice, DEGs were only detected in microglia (Figure 6A), consistent with TPL2 being most highly expressed by microglia in the mouse brain (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by pseudo-bulk differential expression analysis shown in Figure 6A

claims.claim: The most upregulated genes in P301S microglia were consistently upregulated to a lesser extent in P301S;TPL2-KD microglia, including cytokines like Tnf and multiple immediate early genes such as Egr1.
claims.source: Analysis of the protein-coding DEGs showed that the most upregulated genes in P301S microglia were consistently upregulated to a lesser extent in P301S;TPL2-KD microglia, including cytokines like Tnf and multiple immediate early genes (IEGs) such as Egr1 (Figure 6B, C).
claims.evidence: Supported by differential expression analysis shown in Figure 6B and C

claims.claim: A subcluster of microglia (C11) expressing high levels of IEGs was elevated in P301S mice, and this elevation was ameliorated by TPL2-KD.
claims.source: On the other hand, a subcluster of microglia (C11) expressing high levels of IEGs (e.g. Fos, Egr1-3, Atf3) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E) was elevated in P301S mice, and this elevation was ameliorated by TPL2-KD (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis shown in Figure 6E and supplement

claims.claim: IEG expression was upregulated in astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes, OPCs, and VSMCs in P301S mice, but the upregulation was only normalized by TPL2-KD in microglia.
claims.source: Calculation of IEG gene set score for every defined cell type (pseudo-bulk) showed IEG expression was up in astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes, OPCs, and VSMCs, but the upregulation was only normalized by TPL2-KD in microglia (and to some extent in VSMCs, although not statistically significant, Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: Supported by gene set score analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G

claims.claim: IEG expression can be regulated by MAPK signaling pathways and TPL2 is a key regulator of MAPK signaling.
claims.source: As IEG expression can be regulated by MAPK signaling pathways and TPL2 is a key regulator of MAPK signaling (Bahrami and Drabløs, 2016; O'Donnell et al., 2012), these results are consistent with a specific role for TPL2 in TauP301S microglia.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Bahrami and Drabløs, 2016 and O'Donnell et al., 2012

claims.claim: A subcluster of microglia (C20) that was elevated in P301S and normalized by TPL2-KD expressed high levels of MHC class II genes.
claims.source: Another subcluster of microglia (C20) that was elevated in P301S and normalized by TPL2-KD in the P301S mice expressed high levels of MHC (major histocompatibility complex) class II genes (e.g. Cd74, H2-Aa, H2-Ab1, etc.), which are usually expressed by antigen presenting cells and are important for the generation of immune responses via interaction with T-cells (Neefjes et al., 2011; Roche and Furuta, 2015; Figure 6F, Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 6F and supplement, and citations

claims.claim: The reduction of P301S MHCII expressing microglia by TPL2-KD combined with the reduction of infiltrating T-cells and dendritic cells points to a normalization of adaptive immune function in P301S brains.
claims.source: The reduction of P301S MHCII expressing microglia by TPL2-KD in P301S mice combined with the reduction of infiltrating T-cells and dendritic cells points to a normalization of adaptive immune function in P301S brains.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the combined changes in MHCII microglia, T-cells, and dendritic cells

claims.claim: Microglia-mediated synapse elimination has been observed in AD mouse models including P301S mice.
claims.source: As microglia-mediated synapse elimination has been observed in AD mouse models including P301S mice (Hansen et al., 2018; Stephan et al., 2012; Wilton et al., 2019), we quantified synapse density by measuring spine number in sparsely labeled dendrites using GFP expression driven by the Thy1-GFP-M transgene.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Hansen et al., 2018; Stephan et al., 2012; Wilton et al., 2019

claims.claim: P301S;TPL2-KD mice had significantly increased spine density compared to P301S mice.
claims.source: Spine analysis by ex vivo imaging found that P301S;TPL2-KD mice had significantly increased spine density compared to P301S mice (Figure 7A), consistent with potentially reduced microglia removal of spines in P301S;TPL2-KD mice.
claims.evidence: Supported by ex vivo imaging data shown in Figure 7A

claims.claim: TauP301S mice develop neurodegeneration, including ventricle enlargement and brain volume reduction, that can be measured by volumetric MRI.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that TauP301S mice develop neurodegeneration, including ventricle enlargement and brain volume reduction, that can be measured by volumetric MRI (vMRI) (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Dejanovic et al., 2018 and Wu et al., 2019

claims.claim: In WT mice, ventricle volumes stayed stable and neocortex and whole brain volumes increased between 6 and 9 months.
claims.source: In WT mice, ventricle volumes stayed stable and neocortex and whole brain volumes increased between 6 and 9 months, and TPL2 kinase deficiency did not alter the trajectory of the brain volume changes.
claims.evidence: Supported by longitudinal vMRI data

claims.claim: TPL2 kinase deficiency did not alter the trajectory of brain volume changes in WT mice.
claims.source: In WT mice, ventricle volumes stayed stable and neocortex and whole brain volumes increased between 6 and 9 months, and TPL2 kinase deficiency did not alter the trajectory of the brain volume changes.
claims.evidence: Supported by longitudinal vMRI data

claims.claim: P301S mice developed brain atrophy, as indicated by increasing ventricle volumes and decreasing brain volumes between 6 and 9 months.
claims.source: As expected, P301S mice developed brain atrophy, as indicated by increasing ventricle volumes and decreasing brain volumes between 6 and 9 months.
claims.evidence: Supported by longitudinal vMRI data

claims.claim: TPL2-KD significantly ameliorated the ventricle enlargement and brain volume decline in TauP301S mice.
claims.source: Strikingly, TPL2-KD significantly ameliorated the ventricle enlargement and brain volume decline in TauP301S mice (Figure 7B, C), indicating a robust neuroprotective effect of inhibition of TPL2 kinase activity in this mouse model.
claims.evidence: Supported by longitudinal vMRI data shown in Figure 7B and C

claims.claim: Inhibition of TPL2 kinase activity has a robust neuroprotective effect in the TauP301S mouse model.
claims.source: Strikingly, TPL2-KD significantly ameliorated the ventricle enlargement and brain volume decline in TauP301S mice (Figure 7B, C), indicating a robust neuroprotective effect of inhibition of TPL2 kinase activity in this mouse model.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the rescue of brain volume loss

claims.claim: Plasma NfL was strongly increased in P301S mice, but TPL2-KD did not significantly affect NfL levels.
claims.source: However, while plasma NfL was strongly increased in P301S mice, TPL2-KD did not significantly affect NfL levels (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: Supported by plasma NfL measurements shown in Figure 7D

claims.claim: While plasma NfL increases in P301S mice, neuroprotection can be achieved irrespective of NfL levels.
claims.source: This indicates that while plasma NfL increases in P301S mice, neuroprotection can be achieved irrespective of NfL levels.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the dissociation between NfL levels and neuroprotection

claims.claim: TauP301S mice displayed behavioral hyperactivity as indicated by significantly increased total beam breaks, ambulatory bouts, and rearing behavior compared with WT mice.
claims.source: As previously seen (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2019), compared with WT mice, 9-month-old TauP301S mice displayed behavioral hyperactivity as indicated by significantly increased total beam breaks, ambulatory bouts, and rearing behavior.
claims.evidence: Supported by open field test data and citations

claims.claim: TPL2 kinase activity deficiency did not impact the locomotor activity of non-transgenic mice, but prevented the hyperactivity in the tauopathy mice.
claims.source: TPL2 kinase activity deficiency did not impact the locomotor activity of non-transgenic mice, but prevented the hyperactivity in the tauopathy mice (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: Supported by open field test data shown in Figure 7E

claims.claim: P301S mice had somewhat elevated baseline freezing behavior and failed to exhibit an increase in freezing behavior in response to the auditory stimulus in trace fear conditioning test.
claims.source: P301S mice had somewhat elevated baseline freezing behavior, and failed to exhibit an increase in freezing behavior in response to the auditory stimulus, indicating potential learning and memory deficits.
claims.evidence: Supported by trace fear conditioning test data

claims.claim: P301S;TPL2-KD mice showed normal baseline freezing behavior and elevated freezing behavior in response to the tone stimulus in trace fear conditioning test.
claims.source: In contrast, P301S;TPL2-KD mice showed normal baseline freezing behavior and elevated freezing behavior in response to the tone stimulus (Figure 7F).
claims.evidence: Supported by trace fear conditioning test data shown in Figure 7F

claims.claim: Eliminating TPL2 kinase activity rescues behavioral alterations in P301S mice.
claims.source: Thus, in addition to reducing neuroinflammation, and protecting against synapse and neuron loss, eliminating TPL2 kinase activity rescues behavioral alterations in P301S mice.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the combined behavioral data showing rescue of hyperactivity and memory deficits

claims.claim: Multiple aspects of neuroinflammation have been implicated in both preclinical AD models and AD patient brains.
claims.source: Multiple aspects of neuroinflammation have been implicated in both preclinical AD models and AD patient brains, and studies with inhibition of specific neuroinflammation pathways have shown beneficial effects in tauopathy and AD models (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Gate et al., 2020; Heneka et al., 2013; Hong et al., 2016; Ising et al., 2019; Laurent et al., 2017; Li et al., 2019; Liddelow et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018; Ndoja et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claims.claim: Studies with inhibition of specific neuroinflammation pathways have shown beneficial effects in tauopathy and AD models.
claims.source: Multiple aspects of neuroinflammation have been implicated in both preclinical AD models and AD patient brains, and studies with inhibition of specific neuroinflammation pathways have shown beneficial effects in tauopathy and AD models (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Gate et al., 2020; Heneka et al., 2013; Hong et al., 2016; Ising et al., 2019; Laurent et al., 2017; Li et al., 2019; Liddelow et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018; Ndoja et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claims.claim: TPL2 is a master regulator of the peripheral immune system that is expressed by microglia.
claims.source: Here, we focused on TPL2 which, as a master regulator of the peripheral immune system that is expressed by microglia, could have pleiotropic effects on neuroinflammation.
claims.evidence: Supported by prior knowledge and expression data

claims.claim: TPL2 is a key regulator of microglia in the brain, similar to its function in the peripheral immune system.
claims.source: In vitro studies show that similar to its function in the peripheral immune system, TPL2 is also key regulator of microglia in the brain.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the in vitro data showing TPL2 regulation of microglia function

claims.claim: The beneficial effects in the TauP301S mice indicate that modulating immune cell function via eliminating TPL2 kinase activity can be beneficial in a context with chronic neuroinflammation where neurodegeneration gradually occurs over time.
claims.source: In contrast, the beneficial effects in the TauP301S mice indicate that modulating immune cell function via eliminating TPL2 kinase activity can be beneficial in a context with chronic neuroinflammation where neurodegeneration gradually occurs over time.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the contrast between acute injury models and chronic tauopathy model

claims.claim: The partial rescue of brain volume loss in TauP301S mice with TPL2-KD likely corresponds to protection of stressed but functional brain tissue that is being destroyed by the inflammatory response to Tau pathology in the brain.
claims.source: The partial rescue of brain volume loss in TauP301S mice with TPL2-KD likely corresponds to protection of stressed but functional brain tissue that is being destroyed by the inflammatory response to Tau pathology in the brain.
claims.evidence: Speculative interpretation of the brain volume rescue data

claims.claim: Despite ongoing stress from transgenic Tau production, the increased synapse density and brain volume represent preservation of functional neuronal circuits.
claims.source: At the same time it is clear that despite ongoing stress from transgenic Tau production, the increased synapse density and brain volume represent preservation of functional neuronal circuits, as the behavioral phenotypes in P301S were rescued in P301S;TPL2-KD mice, indicating functional benefits.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the correlation between structural preservation and behavioral rescue

claims.claim: The tauopathy model study reveals multiple aspects of pathophysiology that are normalized by TPL2-KD concordant with rescue of neurodegeneration and behavior.
claims.source: The tauopathy model study reveals multiple aspects of pathophysiology that are normalized by TPL2-KD concordant with rescue of neurodegeneration and behavior. This includes reductions of the levels of various cytokines, normalization of increased T-cell and dendritic cell abundance in the brain, and reduction in the IEG and MHCII subpopulations of activated microglia.
claims.evidence: Summarizes the combined findings from the tauopathy study

claims.claim: A recent study found T-cell depletion resulted in a robust reduction of neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in TauP301S mice.
claims.source: In this context, it is notable that a recent study found T-cell depletion resulted in a robust reduction of neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in TauP301S mice (Chen et al., 2023), suggesting that the reduced amount of T-cells in the brains could be particularly relevant to the protective effects of eliminating TPL2 kinase activity.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2023

claims.claim: The reduced amount of T-cells in the brains could be particularly relevant to the protective effects of eliminating TPL2 kinase activity.
claims.source: In this context, it is notable that a recent study found T-cell depletion resulted in a robust reduction of neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in TauP301S mice (Chen et al., 2023), suggesting that the reduced amount of T-cells in the brains could be particularly relevant to the protective effects of eliminating TPL2 kinase activity.
claims.evidence: Speculative inference based on cited study

claims.claim: A recent study found that endothelial TPL2 regulates blood-brain barrier permeability and immune cell infiltration in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model.
claims.source: While TPL2 is most highly expressed in microglia, it is also expressed at fairly high levels in endothelial cells. Interestingly, a recent study has found that endothelial TPL2 regulates blood-brain barrier permeability and immune cell infiltration in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model (Nanou et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Nanou et al., 2021

claims.claim: Conditional KO of TPL2 in endothelial cells but not microglia, astrocytes, or neurons, protected against EAE disease severity.
claims.source: In that study conditional KO of TPL2 in endothelial cells but not microglia, astrocytes, or neurons, protected against EAE disease severity.
claims.evidence: Supported by reference to findings from Nanou et al., 2021

claims.claim: Endothelial TPL2 activation was found to allow immune cell infiltration by promoting degradation of tight junction proteins including Cldn5, without changes in their corresponding mRNAs.
claims.source: Endothelial TPL2 activation was found to allow immune cell infiltration, and this was proposed to function by promoting degradation of tight junction proteins including Cldn5, without changes in their corresponding mRNAs.
claims.evidence: Supported by reference to findings from Nanou et al., 2021

claims.claim: The regulation of T-cell and dendritic cell infiltration into the brain of TauP301S mice could be mediated by TPL2 function in endothelial cells.
claims.source: This raises the possibility that the regulation of T-cell and dendritic cell infiltration into the brain of TauP301S mice could also be mediated by TPL2 function in endothelial cells.
claims.evidence: Speculative inference based on the EAE study findings

claims.claim: Subclustering analysis of endothelial cells identified one subcluster (cluster 7) that increased in proportion in TauP301S mice but was partially normalized in proportion by TPL2-KD in P301S mice.
claims.source: Nevertheless, subclustering analysis of the endothelial cells in our TauP301S scRNA-seq study identified one subcluster (cluster 7) that increased in proportion in TauP301S mice but that was partially normalized in proportion by TPL2-KD in P301S mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 6A,B).
claims.evidence: Supported by scRNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6A,B

claims.claim: Cluster 7 specific marker genes included IEGs such as Ier2/3/5l, Fos, Ubs, and Dusp6.
claims.source: Cluster 7 specific marker genes included IEGs such as Ier2/3/5l, Fos, Ubs, and Dusp6 (Figure 5—figure supplement 6C) (but not Cldn5).
claims.evidence: Supported by marker gene analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 6C

claims.claim: The endothelial cluster 7 data is consistent with TPL2-dependent regulation of the MAPK signaling pathway in endothelial cells in TauP301S mice.
claims.source: While this is consistent with TPL2-dependent regulation of the MAPK signaling pathway in endothelial cells in TauP301S mice, determining whether TPL2 signaling in endothelial cells regulates infiltration of peripheral immune cells in TauP301S mice will require further investigation.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the IEG expression in endothelial cluster 7

claims.claim: TPL2 is expressed in both innate and adaptive immune cells in the peripheral system.
claims.source: Aside from microglia, astrocytes, and endothelial cells in the brain, TPL2 is also expressed in both innate and adaptive immune cells in the peripheral system (Xu et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Xu et al., 2018

claims.claim: Microglia orchestrate both protective and damaging responses during neurodegeneration in conditions such as AD.
claims.source: Microglia orchestrate both protective and damaging responses during neurodegeneration in conditions such as AD (Bohlen et al., 2019; Hansen et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Bohlen et al., 2019 and Hansen et al., 2018

claims.claim: Other recent therapeutic approaches have focused on boosting microglia activation to accelerate clearance of disease-related protein aggregates, such enhancing TREM2-mediated stimulation of microglia phagocytosis of Aβ.
claims.source: While our results support a beneficial role of reducing microglia activation by inhibiting TPL2 in a tauopathy model, other recent therapeutic approaches have focused on boosting microglia activation to accelerate clearance of disease-related protein aggregates, such enhancing TREM2-mediated, stimulation of microglia phagocytosis of Aβ (Fassler et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Fassler et al., 2021 and Wang et al., 2020

claims.claim: Reducing the inflammatory state of the brain with approaches such as targeting TPL2 kinase activity could be a potential therapeutic approach for diseases with chronic neuroinflammation.
claims.source: Overall, our data indicate that reducing the inflammatory state of the brain with approaches such as targeting TPL2 kinase activity could be a potential therapeutic approach for diseases with chronic neuroinflammation.
claims.evidence: Speculative conclusion based on the study findings

claims.claim: Various TPL2-dependent features of neuroinflammation include elevated brain cytokine level peripheral immune cell infiltration, specific activation states of microglia, etc. that could be explored as other potential therapeutic approaches.
claims.source: Our data also highlight that various TPL2-dependent features of neuroinflammation include elevated brain cytokine level peripheral immune cell infiltration, specific activation states of microglia, etc. that could be explored as other potential therapeutic approaches.
claims.evidence: Speculative suggestion based on the study findings

claims.claim: Activation of microglia occurs in numerous neurodegenerative conditions including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), where microglia are activated in response to amyloid and tau pathology.
claims.source: Activation of microglia, the tissue resident macrophages of the brain, occurs in numerous neurodegenerative conditions including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD), where microglia are activated in response to amyloid and tau pathology.
claims.evidence: Established knowledge about microglia activation in neurodegenerative diseases

claims.claim: Microglia activation may facilitate beneficial functions, such as clearance of amyloid plaques, in the early stages of AD.
claims.source: While microglia activation may facilitate beneficial functions, such as clearance of amyloid plaques, in the early stages of AD, chronic microglia activation could contribute to disease progression via cytokine release and other harmful functions during later stages of disease (Bright et al., 2019; Hansen et al., 2018; Leng and Edison, 2021).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Bright et al., 2019; Hansen et al., 2018; Leng and Edison, 2021

claims.claim: Chronic microglia activation could contribute to disease progression via cytokine release and other harmful functions during later stages of AD.
claims.source: While microglia activation may facilitate beneficial functions, such as clearance of amyloid plaques, in the early stages of AD, chronic microglia activation could contribute to disease progression via cytokine release and other harmful functions during later stages of disease (Bright et al., 2019; Hansen et al., 2018; Leng and Edison, 2021).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Bright et al., 2019; Hansen et al., 2018; Leng and Edison, 2021

claims.claim: A pathogenic role for inflammatory cytokines in neurodegeneration is supported by the increased risk for AD in people with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriasis, and other inflammatory diseases.
claims.source: A pathogenic role for inflammatory cytokines in neurodegeneration is supported by the increased risk for AD in people with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriasis, and other inflammatory diseases, and a significantly reduced incidence of AD for those patients that received treatment with TNF blocking agents (Zhou et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2020

claims.claim: There is a significantly reduced incidence of AD for patients with inflammatory diseases that received treatment with TNF blocking agents.
claims.source: A pathogenic role for inflammatory cytokines in neurodegeneration is supported by the increased risk for AD in people with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriasis, and other inflammatory diseases, and a significantly reduced incidence of AD for those patients that received treatment with TNF blocking agents (Zhou et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Zhou et al., 2020

claims.claim: Studies in AD and FTD models identify harmful effects of activated astrocytes.
claims.source: This includes studies in AD and FTD models that identify harmful effects of activated astrocytes (Li et al., 2019), NLRP3 inflammasome activation (Heneka et al., 2013; Ising et al., 2019), complement pathway activation (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Hong et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2019), and infiltration of T-cells (Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018).

claims.claim: Studies in AD and FTD models identify harmful effects of NLRP3 inflammasome activation.
claims.source: This includes studies in AD and FTD models that identify harmful effects of activated astrocytes (Li et al., 2019), NLRP3 inflammasome activation (Heneka et al., 2013; Ising et al., 2019), complement pathway activation (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Hong et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2019), and infiltration of T-cells (Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Heneka et al., 2013 and Ising et al., 2019

claims.claim: Studies in AD and FTD models identify harmful effects of complement pathway activation.
claims.source: This includes studies in AD and FTD models that identify harmful effects of activated astrocytes (Li et al., 2019), NLRP3 inflammasome activation (Heneka et al., 2013; Ising et al., 2019), complement pathway activation (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Hong et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2019), and infiltration of T-cells (Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Dejanovic et al., 2018; Hong et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2019

claims.claim: Studies in AD and FTD models identify harmful effects of infiltration of T-cells.
claims.source: This includes studies in AD and FTD models that identify harmful effects of activated astrocytes (Li et al., 2019), NLRP3 inflammasome activation (Heneka et al., 2013; Ising et al., 2019), complement pathway activation (Dejanovic et al., 2018; Hong et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2019), and infiltration of T-cells (Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Gate et al., 2020; Laurent et al., 2017; Merlini et al., 2018

claims.claim: Targeting a central regulator of inflammatory function represents an attractive therapeutic approach given diverse mediators of the detrimental effects of neuroinflammation and microglia activation.
claims.source: Given such diverse mediators of the detrimental effects of neuroinflammation and microglia activation, targeting a central regulator of inflammatory function represents an attractive therapeutic approach.
claims.evidence: Logical inference from the diversity of neuroinflammation mediators

claims.claim: TPL2 is a kinase that is expressed in both adaptive and innate immune cells in the peripheral system and plays central roles in regulating inflammatory responses.
claims.source: We therefore focused on tumor progression locus 2 (TPL2), a kinase that is expressed in both adaptive and innate immune cells in the peripheral system and plays central roles in regulating inflammatory responses.
claims.evidence: Established knowledge about TPL2

claims.claim: TPL2 is a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase (MAP3K) downstream of TNFR, IL1R, and Toll-like receptors.
claims.source: TPL2 is a mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase (MAP3K) downstream of TNFR, IL1R, and Toll-like receptors.

claims.source: Preclinical studies using genetic manipulation of TPL2 in mice have found that TPL2 deficiency provides beneficial effects in multiple inflammatory disease models, such as inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis, pancreatitis, and multiple sclerosis (Senger et al., 2017; Sriskantharajah et al., 2014; Xiao et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2018), and TPL2 is being pursued as a target for treating inflammatory conditions including RA and psoriasis (Zarrin et al., 2021).

claims.claim: TPL2 regulates microglia inflammatory activity and damage to neurons.
claims.source: These experiments indicate that TPL2 regulates microglia inflammatory activity and damage to neurons, and that blocking TPL2 function can be neuroprotective.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the combined experimental results

claims.claim: Blocking TPL2 function can be neuroprotective.
claims.source: These experiments indicate that TPL2 regulates microglia inflammatory activity and damage to neurons, and that blocking TPL2 function can be neuroprotective.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the combined experimental results showing protection in various models

results.result: TPL2 expression is enriched in brain myeloid cells and endothelial cells, and is upregulated in neuroinflammatory conditions including LPS injection, tauopathy models, and Alzheimer's disease patient brains.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 provide converging evidence from multiple sources (RNA-seq from human and mouse, bulk and sorted cells, protein analysis) showing TPL2 expression patterns in the brain under both homeostatic and disease conditions. The data are supported by appropriate citations and experimental evidence.

results.result: TPL2 mediates MAPK signaling (ERK and p38 phosphorylation) but not NF-κB signaling in microglia following LPS stimulation, as demonstrated by pharmacological inhibition studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C10 are well-supported by Western blot data showing selective effects of TPL2 inhibitors on MAPK pathway components (ERK, p38) but not NF-κB (p65) phosphorylation. The specificity is demonstrated by lack of effects on baseline phosphorylation and selective pathway inhibition.

results.result: TPL2 is a key regulator of proinflammatory cytokine production in microglia, with both pharmacological inhibition and genetic knockout dramatically reducing LPS-induced cytokine release.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C14 demonstrate TPL2's role in cytokine regulation through both pharmacological (inhibitors) and genetic (TPL2-KD mice) approaches. The multiplex immunoassay data showing reduced TNFα, IL-1α, IL-6, and CXCL1 production provide strong convergent evidence.

results.result: TPL2 inhibition protects neurons from microglia-mediated neurotoxicity in co-culture systems, with both pharmacological inhibition and genetic knockout rescuing LPS+IFNγ-induced neuronal loss.
results.evaluation: Claims C15-C18 demonstrate neuroprotection through MAP2 immunostaining in co-culture experiments. Both pharmacological (G-767) and genetic (TPL2-KD microglia) approaches show rescue of neuronal loss, providing strong evidence for TPL2's role in microglia-mediated neurotoxicity.

results.result: TPL2 regulates iNOS expression in activated microglia, and NO production is a key mediator of neuronal death in the co-culture system, as demonstrated by both TPL2 and iNOS inhibition rescuing neurons.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C24 establish a mechanistic link between TPL2, iNOS, and neuronal death. Western blot data show TPL2-dependent iNOS regulation (50% reduction with inhibitor, 85% with genetic knockout), and iNOS inhibitor 1400W rescues neuronal loss, establishing causality.

results.result: In an acute LPS injection model, TPL2-KD mice show attenuated microglia and astrocyte activation, with reduced DAM gene expression, preserved homeostatic microglia genes, normalized proliferation genes, and decreased brain cytokine levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C31 are supported by comprehensive bulk RNA-seq and cytokine measurements showing multiple coordinated changes in TPL2-KD mice following LPS injection. The data demonstrate reduced neuroinflammation across multiple molecular readouts including gene modules and protein levels.

results.result: TPL2-dependent astrocyte activation in vivo is largely mediated indirectly through microglia rather than cell-autonomous astrocyte function, as demonstrated by differential responses in cultured astrocytes versus in vivo LPS studies.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C37 provide evidence for indirect astrocyte activation through comparison of in vitro and in vivo data. The restricted TPL2 dependence in cultured astrocytes versus broader effects in vivo supports the interpretation of indirect activation via microglia-derived factors.

results.result: TPL2-KD reduces microgliosis but does not provide neuroprotection in acute injury models (optic nerve crush and stroke), suggesting that reduced neuroinflammation alone is insufficient for protection in severe acute tissue damage.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C40 demonstrate limitations of TPL2 inhibition in acute injury models. The data show reduced microgliosis without functional benefit (no RGC rescue, no improvement in stroke outcomes), supporting the interpretation that the therapeutic context matters.

results.result: In the TauP301S chronic tauopathy model, TPL2-KD slightly ameliorates gliosis (Iba1 and GFAP), reduces phospho-Tau pathology, and decreases brain cytokine levels including CXCL9, CXCL10, IL6, and IFNγ.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C45 are supported by immunostaining and cytokine measurements in aged TauP301S mice. The data show modest but consistent reductions in multiple inflammatory markers. The reduction in phospho-Tau is noted as potentially reflecting neuroinflammation-tau interplay, appropriately cautious.

results.result: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis reveals that TPL2-KD significantly reduces infiltration of peripheral immune cells (T-cells and dendritic cells) in TauP301S brains, with no effects on cell type proportions in non-transgenic mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C52 are well-supported by scRNA-seq cellularity analysis and validated by IHC. The specificity of effects (only in P301S mice, only T-cells and dendritic cells) strengthens the conclusions. The identification of dendritic cells through subclustering and ImmGen mapping is methodologically sound.

results.result: The reduced presence of peripheral immune cells in TauP301S×TPL2-KD brains could have beneficial effects, based on prior studies showing T-cell presence in AD and beneficial effects of T-cell depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C55 are speculative (C55 explicitly uses 'could have'). While the citations support T-cell presence in AD and benefits of depletion in other models, the actual functional consequences in this specific model are not directly demonstrated here, only inferred from the literature.

results.result: Both CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells are increased in P301S brains and reduced by TPL2-KD, with the CD8.4 subcluster (expressing exhaustion markers Nr4a2 and Pdcd1) being the largest and most affected.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C58 provide detailed characterization of T-cell subtypes through scRNA-seq analysis. The identification of exhaustion markers is supported by appropriate citations, and the cellularity analysis shows consistent effects across T-cell subtypes.

results.result: Pseudo-bulk differential expression analysis shows TPL2-dependent gene expression changes only in microglia within TauP301S mice, with reduced expression of immediate early genes (IEGs) including Tnf and Egr1, and reduced abundance of IEG-expressing microglia subcluster C11.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C63 are supported by comprehensive scRNA-seq analysis including pseudo-bulk DE, subclustering, and gene set scoring. The cell-type specificity (only microglia) is consistent with TPL2 expression patterns. The link to MAPK signaling is appropriately supported by citations.

results.result: TPL2-KD reduces a microglia subcluster (C20) expressing high levels of MHC class II genes, which combined with reduced T-cells and dendritic cells, indicates normalization of adaptive immune function in P301S brains.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C65 are supported by scRNA-seq analysis showing coordinated changes in MHCII-expressing microglia and peripheral immune cells. The interpretation of normalized adaptive immunity is reasonable given the known role of MHCII in T-cell interactions, supported by appropriate citations.

results.result: TPL2-KD significantly increases dendritic spine density in TauP301S mice, consistent with reduced microglia-mediated synapse elimination.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C67 are supported by ex vivo two-photon imaging of Thy1-GFP-labeled neurons. The interpretation of reduced synapse elimination is appropriately cautious ('consistent with potentially reduced') and supported by citations showing microglia-mediated synapse loss in AD models.

results.result: Longitudinal volumetric MRI demonstrates that TPL2-KD significantly ameliorates ventricle enlargement and brain volume decline in TauP301S mice, indicating robust neuroprotection, with no effects on brain volume trajectories in WT mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C73 are strongly supported by longitudinal vMRI data showing significant rescue of brain atrophy. The specificity (no effects in WT mice) and the magnitude of effects (significant amelioration of both ventricle and brain volume changes) provide strong evidence for neuroprotection.

results.result: Plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels are elevated in P301S mice but not affected by TPL2-KD, indicating that neuroprotection can occur independently of NfL levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C75 are supported by plasma NfL measurements. The dissociation between NfL levels and neuroprotection is an important observation, though the interpretation (C75) is somewhat speculative. The authors appropriately note this could reflect ongoing NfL production by protected tissue.

results.result: TPL2-KD rescues behavioral alterations in TauP301S mice, preventing hyperactivity in open field tests and normalizing learning/memory deficits in trace fear conditioning, with no effects on behavior in non-transgenic mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C80 are well-supported by behavioral data from open field and trace fear conditioning tests. The specificity of effects (only in P301S mice) and rescue across multiple behavioral domains (locomotor activity and memory) provide strong evidence for functional benefits.

results.result: The beneficial effects of TPL2-KD in chronic tauopathy (but not acute injury) indicate that modulating immune function can be beneficial in contexts with chronic neuroinflammation and gradual neurodegeneration, likely protecting stressed but functional tissue from inflammatory destruction.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C88 synthesize the findings and provide interpretation. The contrast between acute and chronic models is well-supported by the data. The mechanistic interpretation (C86-C87) is somewhat speculative but reasonable given the combined structural, molecular, and behavioral data.

results.result: Recent studies showing that T-cell depletion reduces neurodegeneration in TauP301S mice suggest that reduced T-cell infiltration could be particularly relevant to TPL2-KD's protective effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C90 rely on a single recent citation (Chen et al., 2023) and are explicitly speculative (C90 uses 'could be'). While the parallel is interesting and the citation is appropriate, the causal contribution of T-cell reduction to the observed benefits is not directly tested in this study.

results.result: TPL2 is expressed in endothelial cells, and prior studies in EAE models show endothelial TPL2 regulates blood-brain barrier permeability and immune cell infiltration. In TauP301S mice, an endothelial subcluster expressing IEGs is partially normalized by TPL2-KD, consistent with TPL2-dependent MAPK signaling in endothelial cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C97 appropriately cite prior work on endothelial TPL2 function but acknowledge that determining whether endothelial TPL2 mediates immune cell infiltration in TauP301S requires further investigation. The endothelial cluster data (C95-C96) are preliminary and the interpretation (C97) is appropriately cautious.

results.result: The study's findings suggest that targeting TPL2 kinase activity could be a potential therapeutic approach for diseases with chronic neuroinflammation, and highlight multiple TPL2-dependent features that could be explored as therapeutic targets.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C102 provide appropriate context and therapeutic implications. The conclusions are appropriately cautious (using 'could be' and 'potential'), acknowledge alternative approaches (C100), and are well-supported by the comprehensive data showing benefits in the chronic tauopathy model.

results.result: Background knowledge establishes that microglia activation occurs in neurodegenerative diseases and may have both beneficial (early amyloid clearance) and harmful (chronic cytokine release) effects, with inflammatory cytokines implicated in AD pathogenesis based on epidemiological studies of inflammatory diseases and TNF blocker treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C107 provide appropriate background context supported by relevant citations. These establish the rationale for studying neuroinflammation modulation in neurodegeneration and are well-established in the field.

results.result: Background on TPL2 establishes it as a MAP3K expressed in immune cells that regulates inflammatory responses via ERK1/2 and p38 activation, with beneficial effects of TPL2 deficiency demonstrated in multiple inflammatory disease models, and rationale for using TPL2-KD rather than KO mice to avoid confounding effects on ABIN-2.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C119 provide comprehensive background on TPL2 biology and the rationale for the experimental approach. The choice of TPL2-KD over KO mice (C119) is well-justified by appropriate citations showing ABIN-2 destabilization in KO mice.

results.result: Summary conclusion that TPL2 regulates microglia inflammatory activity and neuronal damage, and that blocking TPL2 function can be neuroprotective.
results.evaluation: Claims C120-C121 appropriately summarize the overall findings from the combined in vitro, acute in vivo, and chronic tauopathy studies. The conclusions are well-supported by the comprehensive experimental evidence presented throughout the manuscript.
